name: S00 DECLARED SURVIVOR — a never-paid payout cell mis-transcribed, with the config pin regenerated
guard: THIS IS THE REPOSITORY'S TOP RESIDUAL, DECLARED RATHER THAN PRETENDED KILLED. Both WTF 1000x tail cells (slots 0 and 13) are among the 80 of 365 payout-table cells the capture never landed on. This mutation changes them to 990, regenerates the config SHA-256 pin in src/config.ts, and propagates the new pin to every chapter that publishes it — i.e. it produces the tree a mis-transcription present from the first commit would have produced. Result: 17 of the 21 scored steps still PASS; FOUR steps reject it — Steps 5, 10, 16 and 17 — declared here as expectFail: [5, 10, 16, 17], so the battery requires exactly those failures to occur and rejects any other. Step 7 can only check cells that actually paid; Step 19's symmetry holds because both mirror cells moved together; Steps 15 and 21 measure the captured drops, none of which landed on those cells. Step 10 rejects it for TWO reasons, and the second is the one real detection in this list. (a) Staleness: the committed outputs/rtp-claim-table.json and its pin (src/rtp-settings.ts) were generated from the original table, so the per-setting table this run computes no longer equals the committed copy — the same kind of rejection as Steps 16 and 17. (b) Detection: with both tails at 990x the WTF board returns 8090/8192 = 98.7548828125%, more than 0.1 pp below the 99% LIQD's Plinko page shows (evidence/rtp-page-labels-2026-10-01.json), so the enforced published-RTP rule (RTP-CLAIM 1.1.0, src/rtp-claim.ts) fails Step 10 on the house side of its band. (b) does not depend on any committed copy: had the cell been 990 from the first commit, the table would have been generated from it and would match, and Step 10 would still fail. What the rule cannot see is a mis-transcription that keeps every board at or above 98.9% (e.g. 1000 -> 997 gives WTF 98.92578125%, inside the band) or one in the player's favour, which the rule never fails. Before 2026-10-01, when the rule was switched on for this package, Step 10's model anchor recomputed the binomial RTP against an exhaustive path enumeration of the SAME table, so both sides moved together and agreed, and Step 10 passed. Steps 5, 16 and 17 are NOT detection. Step 17: the committed outputs/simulation-results.json was produced with the original table, so the payout-weighted z values it stores no longer re-derive (max |delta| 1.56e-2 against a 1e-9 tolerance). Step 16: it recomputes each row's theoretical RTP from the pinned plinkoConfig.json instead of reading the artifact's own theory column, and the recomputed 13r/4 theory (0.987548828125) no longer equals the committed column (0.989990234375); `simRTP within 6 SE of the RECOMPUTED theory` still reports 28/28, i.e. the SIMULATED numbers do not object. Step 5: it runs the ProvablyFair.org site verifier, whose paytables.js is a hash-pinned copy of the ORIGINAL plinkoConfig.json (the site file says it was generated from it), so the edited config no longer equals the pinned copy on the two WTF tail cells — a second anchor on the committed table, not detection: had the original transcription been wrong, the site copy generated from it would carry the same error. Had the cell been wrong from the first commit, the simulation would have been run with the wrong table and Steps 16 and 17 would agree too. So the residual narrows to errors that stay inside the published-RTP band: nothing in this repository can tell a correct transcription of a never-paid cell from a wrong one that leaves every board at or above 98.9%. Closing it needs the operator's client bundle chunk or a hashed get-game-settings response carrying the tables committed as evidence; see MANIFEST 'Residual (declared)' and Recommendations. History: reported as M3a by the round-1 external review; 21/21 at round 2; 18/21 after Step 16 (round 4) and Step 5 (2026-09-24) joined — both artifact staleness; 17/21 since 2026-10-01, when the enforced RTP-CLAIM rule added Step 10. Two further things notice the edit for the same artifact-staleness reason and are equally not detection: the derived emission guard in verify.ts (outputs/coverage-results.json carries each configuration's never-observed RTP share, which moves with the table) and, on a mocha run, the RTP pins in tests/plinko/rtpPinTests.ts — which pin OUR transcription, so a value wrong from the first commit would have been pinned along with it.
